transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function for the Rust 1.96 target body.
Adapted the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &[T]` parameter, removed `const`, and named the return value for Verus; no target-body path was externalized or assumed.

Lowered the unsupported Rust slice pattern `if let [init @ .., last] = self` to the mechanically equivalent nonempty branch `slice.len() != 0`, `slice.split_at(slice.len() - 1)`, and `&tail[0]`; this preserves the init-prefix/last-element data flow of the Rust body while using Verus-supported syntax.

Added proof-only `lemma_split_at` and view equality assertions connecting the desugared init/tail views to the generated `slice@[(slice@.len() - 1) as int]` and `slice@.subrange(0, slice@.len() - 1)` contract; these annotations do not change executable control flow or data flow.
